discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This was a theoretical prediction followed by a decisive experiment. It created the field of moiré quantum matter, which is now realised in many platforms: twisted multilayer graphene, transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures (which host fractional Chern insulators), and optical and cold-atom analogues. It gives physicists a tunable laboratory for strong correlations, topology and quantum geometry, the last of which turns out to set the superfluid weight in flat bands. Few discoveries of the past two decades have opened such a broad and lasting research direction, bringing together band topology, correlated electrons and superconductivity.
